In other words, meeting these gaps requires innovative approaches, and artificial intelligence (AI) pops up as a promising tool enabling the transformative change that is required. The current research paper aims to delve into the intersection of equitable access to education and AI in pursuit of throwing its light on how AI technologies can offer tools to level the ground in primary education easily and hence bridge the divide. This paper begins by capturing the multifarious nature of educational inequities, such as socioeconomic, geographical, cultural, disability, and many others. This article does that through case studies and empirical evidence of how AI-enabled initiatives have already closed the gap in primary learning opportunities, empowering learners regardless of the socioeconomic background or geographical location.

articleTitle: A Strategic Layout Design for Creating Prediction System for Heart Related Disease Using Hms
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Advance Computing and Innovative Technologies in Engineering (ICACITE)
abstract: In light of the increasing flood of organized and unstructured data, combined with fast advancements in analysis methods, Intelligent technology (AI) is bringing in a new age for the healthcare business. However, the widespread inclusion of AI in the healthcare sector provides rise to reservations regarding openness, explainability, and possible flaws inherent in predictions from the model. Resolving these concerns, Explainable intelligent machines (XAI) appears as a crucial answer, improving the reliability of AI systems among both physicians and academics. This heightened credibility, in turn, promotes a more broad and responsible usage of AI in healthrelated situations. This paper attempts to shed light on the different interpretability methods, acting as a complete guide for practitioners looking to understand and interpret explainable autonomous systems. In the setting of medical services, where model results directly affect human lives, the urge for openness is important. Drawing upon cases from a cardiovascular disorder dataset, our paper stresses the importance of employing simplicity techniques to build trust in practitioners whenever utilizing artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms for medical evaluations. By giving insights onto the comprehensibility of these mathematical models, this dissertation aims to add to the creation of a trustworthy basis for the inclusion of computer vision in healthcare.

Author Keywords: Example based Techniques and Feature based Techniques

articleTitle: A Way to Design Data Transfer System Modelling to Secure and Transmit Data with the Help of Fuzzy Based Logic in Healthcare System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Advance Computing and Innovative Technologies in Engineering (ICACITE)
abstract: Healthcare utilization of data plays a key part in cancer types and disease prediction. Bringing fuzzy linear regression algorithms into dynamic analysis improves decision-making in medical business, especially for dynamic analyses of data. To handle issues linked to computing intricacy and processing time and energy, a convex hull method is suggested, focused on using the Beneath-Beyond algorithm. This gradual method lowers computing speed and complexity, reducing current limits. Using a real fuzzy medicinal products dataset compared to the industry, the study includes creating an offering of fuzzy numerical optimization alongside applying the convex hull method to obtain coordinate points in hyper-rectangles circles. This combo results in a new convex hull-based flexible linear equation model designed for dynamic curved health care data. This improved program aims to quicken processes of decision-making, especially among critical healthcare areas, giving a useful addition to the field.

articleTitle: The AI Based Design Layout for Exploring the Reader Experience through Technical Interaction for Learning Literature
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Advance Computing and Innovative Technologies in Engineering (ICACITE)
abstract: The domain where Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Literature meet, it’s quite an interesting area of study; it brings with itself a totally different way of authoring a text and the participation of the reader.” In this paper, we discuss the newly developing domain of AIgenerated literature and its reader interaction implications. In our paper, “AI Writes, You Decide: Exploring Reader Interaction in AI-Generated Literature,” we delve into the ways readers engage with AI-authored literary works. We first try to outline the current landscape of AI -generated literature, focusing on the most significant achievements, challenges, and ethical issues. Whether that be the poetry of an algorithm or an AI-authored novel, more and more literature is being sourced from AI, raising questions surrounding the value human creativity places on them and the intentions and relatedness to authorship that comprise the making of the literary work. We try to analyze how readers’ relation to AI-generated texts takes on a new guise, grounded on an interdisciplinary approach. This is opposed to what is seen in traditional literature, where the relation between the readers and the author is said to be paradigmatic. AIgenerated literature, however, completely inverts that relation: readers do not have any idea about a priori authorial presence; they simply keep moving through a jungle of narrative. We will analyze both quantitatively and qualitatively the readers’ answers regarding several issues, such as emotional engagement, interpretative freedom, and authenticity perception when dealing with an AI-generated text. Moreover, the paper touches on how readers’ feedback could influence AI-generated literature. Normally, the feedback is one-way from the author to the reader in the dyad relation of author-reader traditional relations.

articleTitle: Ai Along with Strategic Competitive System for Developing Early Adopters and Market Positioning System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Advance Computing and Innovative Technologies in Engineering (ICACITE)
abstract: Recent years have seen the emergence of several advanced technologies, artificial intelligence (AI) in particular, and, in turn, its integration has long been considered one of the pivotal factors to derive strategic competitive advantage. The current study discusses the dynamics of AI adoption and its relationship with market positioning strategies among the first movers. With this background, this research is intended to bring out how various companies in different industries tend to put AI into better use to gain a competitive edge and effectively place themselves in the market. This, in a brief sense, depicts a mixed-method approach, in which qualitative interviews are integrated with a quantitative analysis of the market data, largely aimed at exploring the effect of the relationship between AI adoption and strategic positioning. Some of the companies identified were interviewed, where early adoption of AI was being referred to by the executives and the decision-makers, in order to understand the key drivers and challenges, and outcomes of integrating AI. To further quantify the relationship between the adoption of AI technology and competitive positioning, the following quantitative analysis for this relationship was done in terms of market performance metrics, such as market share, revenue growth, and profitability.

articleTitle: Hybrid Fuzzy Decision-Making Model
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Advance Computing and Innovative Technologies in Engineering (ICACITE)
abstract: Establishing a sustainable the healthcare system necessitates the development of social, economic, and environmental norms. Although many studies concentrate on these elements separately, an integrated method of handling evaluating environmentally friendly development in healthcare institutions is conspicuously lacking. To address this gap, this paper presents a technique for studying indicators of sustainable development in healthcare organizations by modifying dimensions, criteria, and characteristics. In all, the three sustainability aspects are covered by the study with 62 traits and 15 criteria identified. Furthermore, a unique implementation technique is proposed to enable this methodology to be applied to real-world issues. This paper makes three contributions: it provides a new methodology for gathering basic data to measure long-term viability levels in healthcare systems; it presents the ability to identify implementation weaknesses in sustainability aspects; and it determines the sustainability level of the healthcare system under imprecise conditions. The study findings provide practitioners and specialists with significant perspectives to assess the sustainability levels of healthcare systems and improve their overall efficacy.

articleTitle: IoT-Enabled Health Monitoring System for Safeguarding Vital Organs with Cloud-Based Diagnosis and Advanced Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Advance Computing and Innovative Technologies in Engineering (ICACITE)
abstract: This study presents a novel IoT-enabled fitness tracking device intended to improve patient care through the capture of real-time physiological records and predictive analytics. The system uses a variety of sensors, including an Arduino UNO, an LM35, a MAX30100 pulse charge and SPo2 sensor, and a stress sensor, to continuously gather health data from ten different patients. Proactive health assessments and early intervention are made possible by the combination of cloud-based analysis and advanced system learning models, such as Support Vector Machines (SVM), Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN), and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN). Tested on real-world datasets, the experimental results show how effective the device is at making accurate and timely predictions. Notably, SVM is the most accurate variant, closely followed by ANN, KNN, and RNN. The confusion matrices ensure accurate and thorough examination of each version’s performance, aiding in selecting the most relevant set of rules for real-time health monitoring to be used by clinicians. The present study, as groundbreaking work, demonstrates a major leap in merging IoT with device expertise in the healthcare sector that usages new possibilities in proactive and personalized treatment strategies. The recommended tool’s innovative and reliable predictive analytics can potentially revolutionize patient transportation in the healthcare system.
